A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VMT-IGMs typographic-attack study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite retitling and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original CLIP Score, FID, defense-detection, and ablation results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results in Tables 2–10, quantitative plots, and generated-image examples, including the appendices.

M1.justification: Typographic-image construction and the pretrained generation procedure remain unchanged. v2 explicitly includes text conditioning in the CLIP description and pseudocode, but image and text inputs were already present in v1's Figure 1 and Section 3.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 37,000-example VMT-IGMs collection derived from 1,000 CelebA-HQ images. Photographic style transfer, full-body generation, typographic-factor variations, and visible/invisible threat scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated model and defense sets are unchanged: UnCLIP, IP-Adapter with SD1.5/SDXL/FLUX, SD3 and Emu2 checks, five prompt-detection methods, the safety checker, and the 'ignore text' defense. Added citations introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated prompts, sample counts, image resolution, typographic settings, clean-image controls, and CLIP Score/FID evaluation remain unchanged. Appendix experiments retain their original settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the same factor sensitivity analyses, invisible-typography tests, prompt-modification ablation, and SD3/Emu2 investigations. No additional robustness test, ablation, or case study is reported.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and across-model averages without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 2–10 and quantitative Figures 6–7 are identical after matching relocated content. Generated-image examples and the reported experimental trends are also retained.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 revises the feature definition from f = CLIP(x) to f = CLIP(x, p), and Algorithm 1 adds f_p to the reverse-process arguments. This is a limited revision of the formal conditioning description; diffusion equations remain unchanged and no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain typographic vulnerability through image inputs, inadequate existing defenses, and VMT-IGMs as an evaluation benchmark. The revised title and expanded conclusion preserve these contributions and the previously stated novelty claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.5.2 replaces categorical failure on bias/neutral concepts with lower detection relative to 'naked' and explicitly includes 'bloody' among poorly detected concepts. This better qualifies the unchanged Table 4 results, whose average detection rates include 16.6% for 'naked' and 4.0% for 'bloody'.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies explicit code-repository and dataset-access links on its title page. This adds resource-location information; the experimental implementation settings otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 revises its threat taxonomy and supporting references, adding works such as RT-Attack and Multimodal Pragmatic Jailbreak while removing some membership-inference and generative-model references. The overall positioning around overlooked vision-modality threats remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, reformats affiliation text, edits the abstract and several explanatory passages, standardizes terminology, adds specific appendix cross-references, and expands the conclusion. The section organization and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: All ten figures and ten tables are retained, with limited caption/header edits and layout changes. Table 3 moves from PDF page 8 to page 7, the title page is reformatted, and appendix reflow leaves a short continuation on an otherwise nearly blank PDF page 13.

improvement.justification: The new code/dataset links improve resource-location guidance, and the revised safety-checker interpretation better reflects Table 4's nonzero detection rates. These limited gains in usability and precision outweigh the small layout regression from the nearly blank appendix page. The experimental evidence remains unchanged.
